text:
Priya: heads-up — control-plane alert for us-west1-gpu clusters. etcd leader flapping and apiserver 5xx spike. controller-manager has restarted a few times. seeing scheduling failures for GPU pods.

Alex: when did it start? I'm seeing leader election churn in etcd around 12:00 UTC. network retransmits between masters increased.

Jake: confirmed. kubectl from bastion shows apiserver crashloops on master-1. quick snapshot:```
$ kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide
NAME                                 READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
etcd-us-west1-0                      1/1     Running            6          14h
apiserver-us-west1-0                 0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   9          3h
controller-manager-us-west1-0       1/1     Running            3          12h
```

Maria: logs look like repeated etcd leader change messages and long GC pauses. snippet:```
W0321 12:01:02.123 etcdserver: leader changed (old: 1, new: 2)
E0321 12:01:03.456 kube-apiserver: etcdserver: request timed out
E0321 12:01:03.789 controller-manager: failed to sync object: timeout waiting for the condition
```

Priya: GPU scheduling impact: several training jobs are pending with "no healthy nodes" or apiserver timeouts. One customer stack reported degraded throughput.

Alex: immediate hypothesis: transient network partition between masters (us-west1-a/b) plus heavier apiserver request load from scale tests. Bumping etcd timeouts may mask root cause.

Jake: agree. action plan I propose: (1) increase etcd election timeout from 1s->3s on masters (safe short-term), (2) temporarily reduce API QPS from internal telemetry agents (can throttle via frontend), (3) cordon a subset of GPU worker nodes to stop new scheduling while control plane stabilizes, (4) redirect non-critical customer traffic to us-east1 as graceful fallback.

Maria: note: doing (4) will increase egress/cross-region cost and could break data locality for some customers. need approval from ops-biz for failover if we hit >10% job loss.

Priya: opened incident and paged oncall. @Alex can you run the etcd health check and post endpoint latencies? also paste the etcd member list.

Alex: running now.```
$ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.10.1.2:2379 member list
8f3a2c... : name=master-0 peerURLs=https://10.10.1.2:2380 clientURLs=https://10.10.1.2:2379 isLeader=false
4b7d1e... : name=master-1 peerURLs=https://10.10.1.3:2380 clientURLs=https://10.10.1.3:2379 isLeader=true
9c2f5b... : name=master-2 peerURLs=https://10.10.1.4:2380 clientURLs=https://10.10.1.4:2379 isLeader=false

$ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... endpoint status --write-out=table
ENDPOINT           ID       STATUS    RAFT_TERM   LEADER   DB_SIZE   IS_LEADER
10.10.1.3:2379     4b7d1e  healthy   42          4b7d1e   12 MB     true
10.10.1.2:2379     8f3a2c  healthy   42          4b7d1e   11 MB     false
10.10.1.4:2379     9c2f5b  healthy   42          4b7d1e   11 MB     false
```

Alex: latencies spiked intermittently: p99 ~ 1.2s for a few minutes, then dropped. network graphs show packet loss ~0.8% between master-1 and master-2 at the time.

Jake: since leader is stable now, still seeing apiserver OOMKill traces on master-1 earlier — process memory ballooned then got restarted by kubelet. probable memory leak or bursty requests.

Priya: temporary mitigations we've executed: (a) reduced telemetry QPS from 1500->200, (b) cordoned gpu-worker-2/3 (drain scheduled for low-priority only), (c) increased kube-apiserver request-timeout in LB to 10s, (d) scaled an additional apiserver replica in us-west to absorb traffic (keeping in readonly mode).

Maria: long-term items to track: - run memory profiling on apiserver - add connection-level metrics for etcd client latencies - enhance cross-AZ network monitoring - add automatic region redirect policy in Redwood Console with cost estimate - evaluate dedicated etcd clusters per-region vs quorum across AZs (tradeoff: durability vs latency)

Priya: cost note from finance POV: failing over significant workloads to another region can add 20-40% infra egress and cross-region VM costs and burn through our reserved GPU capacity buffers. If we go to on-demand spare capacity (for fast failover) we'll incur ~0.3x the monthly committed cost. We need product signoff if we push customers across regions automatically.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-234; severity=P2; escalation=requested -> oncall@redwood. (react: :rotating_light:)

deploy-bot: Rollout blocked: cannot deploy apiserver-bump-1.3 because cluster has pending control-plane restarts. Reason: k8s-health-check failed.

Alex: next steps for oncall: run apiserver heap dump if it recurs, capture pprof, and collect strace if OOM kills continue. Ops: prepare a cost estimate for cross-region fallback (Maria/Jake). Priya: can you post the runbook link and owner?

Priya: runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/k8s-control-plane. Owner: @Priya (oncall lead) and @Maria (network). I'm assigning follow-ups in the incident ticket.

Jake: I'll keep an eye on GPU scheduling once etcd stabilizes. If we still see >5% pending for 10m, escalate to exec and flip regional routing.

Priya: thanks all. keep updates here — small, frequent notes preferred. (react: :thumbsup:)
